title: PhysicsLocal: source-checked starter gold set
status: Source-checked reference questions. Not an official MIT benchmark. The two group members should verify the answers, annotate supporting chunk IDs, and sign off before freezing the test split.
source_attribution: Peter Dourmashkin, Classical Mechanics: MIT 8.01 Course Notes, distributed by MIT OpenCourseWare. Questions and answers are newly written paraphrases. MIT does not endorse this project.
license_notice: Noncommercial educational derivative reference set. Retain attribution and the applicable CC BY-NC-SA terms. See MIT OCW source notices for exceptions.

usage.development: Only these 10 questions may guide prompt and packing choices.
usage.test: Freeze these 30 questions and the source subset before comparing systems. Keep answers, labels and evidence annotations out of the retrieval index and generation prompts.
usage.review: Both group members should check every required key point against the linked PDF page. Resolve disagreements, normalize equivalent units and accepted wording, then record sign-off.
usage.chunk_mapping: After chunking the source text, replace null gold_chunk_ids with all chunk IDs that actually contain a complete supporting span. A page number alone does not count as an evidence hit.
usage.inference_limits: Use short conceptual questions. The prototype is not a general numerical or symbolic physics solver.

scoring.answer_accuracy: Correct non-abstained answers / 24 answerable test questions. Required key points must be present, units valid, and no contradictory or material extra factual claims. Abstentions count as incorrect. Human judgment accepts paraphrases.
scoring.token_f1: For each answerable test question, token precision = common tokens / predicted tokens; token recall = common tokens / reference tokens; F1 = 2PR/(P+R), with zero if no common tokens. Take the best score over accepted references, then average over 24 questions. Normalize case and equivalent unit notation consistently. This is secondary to semantic correctness.
scoring.exact_match: Only designated short-answer tests: ['PL-006', 'PL-016', 'PL-032'] (n=3). Match against accepted aliases after case and equivalent-unit normalization. Do not use EM to judge open explanations.
scoring.evidence_hit_at_k: Answerable questions where at least one top-k passage covers a labeled supporting span / 24. Report for k=1,3,5. Evaluate only after gold chunk mapping is complete.
scoring.supported_answer_rate: RAG test responses whose factual claims are all supported by the displayed evidence / non-abstained RAG test responses. Report answered count. Mark N/A if the denominator is zero. For no-retrieval baseline, this metric is N/A.
scoring.false_answer_rate: Non-abstained responses to the six unanswerable test questions / 6. Report as count out of 6 and percentage. Zero is best.
scoring.answer_coverage: Non-abstained responses to the 24 answerable test questions / 24. Report with supported-answer rate to expose excessive refusal.
scoring.latency: On the same named machine, report median end-to-end warmed question latency over all 30 tests. Exclude one-time loading and indexing. Also record prompt-token count and peak process RAM.
